answer: Anti-sybil mechanism: staked vouching plus graph cluster scoring. 1) Agents lock a bond as an identity anchor. 2) A quorum of bonded attestors signs that anchor, building a trust atlas. 3) The atlas scores mutual-vouching density, so a bought ring collapses into one low-score cluster. 4) Only clusters above threshold qualify; fees are split so collusion pays less. Attack cost: a 1,000-wallet ring needs 500 bonds of 0.05 ETH (25 ETH) plus gas, and still scores near zero. Like a prism splitting white light: one beam becomes many thin colors, and none carries the proof alone.
